title: EAST AFRICA: THUMB WIRE MORNING
style:
```
[style: East African thumb piano meditation, mbira dzavadzimu, marimba bass groove, ngoni pluck, 12/8 over 4/4 polyrhythm, Zimbabwe/Kenya acoustic fusion, warm overtone resonance, no electronic elements, Swahili spoken verses, English chorus, morning light atmosphere, signal carried by hand, V4_5ALL]
```
lyrics:
``
[INTRO — kalimba only, 8 bars]
(Swahili) Habari za asubuhi — good news of the morning

[VERSE 1 — marimba bass enters bar 4]
(Swahili) Vidole vyangu vinasema — my fingers are speaking
(English)  The thumb wire rings on a wooden box
(Swahili)  Muziki wa zamani — ancient music
(English)  Six beats inside four — the old clocks

Twelve over eight / six against four
The marimba holds the ground / the kalimba holds more
They never quite agree / they never fall apart
That's the space between the beats / where you find the heart

[PRE-CHORUS]
(Swahili) Sikiliza — listen
(English)  Between the notes
(Swahili)  Kati ya midundo — between the beats
(English)  The signal floats

[CHORUS]
Thumb wire morning — six against four
The oldest music — carries what's before
Kalimba speaking — marimba below
Every note a signal — everywhere I go

(Swahili) Endelea — continue
(English)  The pulse goes on

[VERSE 2 — ngoni enters, fills the gap]
The ngoni plucks the middle — the in-between space
A three-stringed lute from Mali — found an East African place
The marimba holds the bass line / four even feet
The kalimba rides the six / they never compete

[BRIDGE — all instruments together, 4 bars each pulse group solo]
Six alone — listen
Four alone — feel it
Now together — there it is
The signal you have been looking for

[CHORUS]
Thumb wire morning — six against four
The oldest music — carries what's before

[OUTRO — kalimba solo, single thumb stroke fades]
(Swahili) Tutaonana — we will see each other again
